category_title: Students with learning difficulties and attention issues who reset tasks when challenged
student_description: Student A is a Year 4 student who struggles with intrinsic motivation and mental calculations, often resetting tasks entirely when faced with challenging sums to avoid failure. He uniquely requires consistent external prompting, concrete physical aids (like rulers or number lines), and explicit permission to skip hard questions to maintain engagement and prevent task avoidance.

criteria.rationale: While the student currently needs heavy external prompting, long-term success requires slowly building his capacity for independent work.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes a strategy to systematically vary, scaffold, or gradually reduce the level of physical, verbal, or visual prompting over time.

criteria.rationale: Because the student lacks intrinsic motivation for challenging math tasks, he needs a reliable external motivator upon completion to sustain engagement over weeks or months.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates a structured reward system where the student earns a preferred activity (e.g., free-choice games) only after completing the required challenging task.
